question: Why does the choice of the muscle site affect how fast a drug works?

options.A: Thicker muscles destroy the active drug ingredients
options.B: Some muscle fibers actively push the medicine out
options.C: Certain sites completely block liquid absorption
options.D: Different muscles have different levels of blood supply

explanation: Blood flow drives absorption speed, so a site with poor circulation will slow down how fast the drug enters the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h1)

question: Why is a family often called a mini-economy when it comes to food?

options.A: Because households must carefully manage limited resources to secure daily meals.
options.B: Because families set the tax rates on imported agricultural products.
options.C: Because households export surplus food to international markets.
options.D: Because families print their own currency to buy groceries.

explanation: You got it! Just like a big economy, a family has to balance its money and resources against the everyday need to put food on the table. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T031#GNS227_U2_T031_h1)

question: How does an additive drug interaction work?

options.A: The combined effect equals the sum of individual effects
options.B: The drugs completely destroy each other in the bloodstream
options.C: The combined effect is lower than either single drug
options.D: The combined effect is much greater than individual effects

explanation: An additive effect is straightforward: 1 + 1 = 2! The drugs simply add their normal effects together without extra superpowers. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T6#GNS125_U5_T6_h2)

question: What should the treatment team do if a patient experiences behavioral instability during trial leave?

options.A: Ban the family from ever visiting again
options.B: Immediately discharge the patient permanently as a penalty
options.C: Ignore the incident and pretend the leave went smoothly
options.D: Analyze the triggers, adjust the care plan, and postpone further leave until stable

explanation: A rough patch isn't a failure—it's valuable feedback! It helps the team adjust the care plan before trying community living again. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h8)

question: In healthcare, what does EHR 'interoperability' mean?

options.A: Patients can print their own paper charts at home using a printer
options.B: All nurses in a hospital use the exact same brand of computer mouse
options.C: Hospital beds automatically update patient weight into the database
options.D: Different health information systems can exchange data accurately

explanation: You got it! Interoperability just means different computer systems can talk to each other and share info smoothly. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is an important nursing duty before an endoscopy procedure begins?

options.A: Ensuring the informed consent form is signed and placed in the chart
options.B: Prescribing the specific dose of sedative drugs for the doctor
options.C: Repairing any broken fibre-optic cables on the camera
options.D: Performing the actual surgical scope insertion in the clinic

explanation: As a nurse, we double-check that the doctor has explained everything and that the signed consent form is safely in the patient's records before they go in. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T2#GNS221_U2_T2_h4)

question: A patient has a long-standing infection that cuts down blood supply, making the affected cells shrink. What is this adaptation called?

options.A: Hyperplasia
options.B: Atrophy
options.C: Hypertrophy
options.D: Metaplasia

explanation: Atrophy is when cells shrink and get smaller due to less work, poor blood supply, or chronic illness. Think of it as cells downsizing! [learn more](GST114_U2_T3#GST114_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is an epidemiological 'reservoir'?

options.A: The natural habitat where an infectious agent normally lives and multiplies
options.B: The chemical disinfectant applied to counter harmful pathogens
options.C: The protective antibodies built up inside a patient's bloodstream
options.D: The medical equipment used to sterilize hospital surgical instruments

explanation: Think of a reservoir as home sweet home for the germ—where it hangs out, grows, and thrives over time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T78#GNS214_U1_T78_h5)

question: What is a major benefit of tele-health for patients living far away from city hospitals?

options.A: Instant physical surgery performed over the internet
options.B: Reduced travel distance and expense to see a specialist
options.C: Guaranteed free smartphones provided by hospitals
options.D: Elimination of all chronic diseases without medication

explanation: Spot on! Tele-health saves patients the stress, time, and transport money of traveling long distances just for a quick consultation. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T6#GNS113_U3_T6_h6)

question: Which powerful antifungal drug is famous for causing severe kidney issues and shaking chills during an IV infusion?

options.A: Terbinafine
options.B: Clotrimazole
options.C: Fluconazole
options.D: Amphotericin B

explanation: That's right! Nurses often call it 'Amphotericin B' (or 'Ampho-terrible' in clinical ward gist) because it saves lives from severe fungal infections, but it's tough on the kidneys and makes patients shake. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T3#GNS215_U6_T3_h3)

question: What is the main biological goal of giving someone a vaccine?

options.A: To provide permanent physical barriers like thickened skin
options.B: To kill all normal flora bacteria residing in the gut
options.C: To stimulate memory cells without causing severe disease
options.D: To permanently disable the patient's innate immune response

explanation: Vaccines give your immune system a safe rehearsal. They train your adaptive memory cells so you're ready if the real germ ever shows up. [learn more](GST114_U4_T1#GST114_U4_T1_h8)

question: A patient with untreated hypothyroidism will most likely show which sign?

options.A: Increased core body temperature
options.B: Decreased basal metabolic rate
options.C: Excessive weight loss despite high appetite
options.D: Rapid resting heart rate

explanation: Thyroid hormones are like your body's engine speed. Without enough of them, everything slows down—giving you a low metabolic rate, weight gain, and feeling cold all the time. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T2#GNS223_U7_T2_h1)

question: What is the primary responsibility of a clinical pharmacist on the health team?

options.A: Helping patients regain physical mobility after a stroke
options.B: Managing home discharge and financial aid resources
options.C: Diagnosing new illnesses and performing surgeries
options.D: Checking drug interactions and safe medication dispensing

explanation: Spot on! Pharmacists are our drug experts. They double-check dosages and interactions to make sure our patients stay safe from medication errors. [learn more](GST321_U7_T2#GST321_U7_T2_h3)

question: Where is the third ventricle located?

options.A: Within the central canal of the lumbar spinal cord
options.B: Directly beneath the outer surface of the occipital lobe
options.C: Inside the core tissue of the cerebellum
options.D: Between the left and right halves of the thalamus

explanation: You're doing great! The third ventricle sits right in the middle, snuggled between the left and right sides of the thalamus. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T9#GNS211_U3_T9_h3)

question: Your CBI patient has bright red drainage and is crying out with severe lower tummy cramps. What's the most likely issue?

options.A: Rapid healing of the surgical wound inside the bladder
options.B: A blocked catheter trapping fluid and blood clots
options.C: A normal reaction to room-temperature saline solution
options.D: An allergic reaction to the antiseptic skin wipes

explanation: Think of it like a clogged sink: fluid keeps pouring in, but nowhere to go. This stretches the bladder and causes painful cramps. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T23#GNS212_U1_T23_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of health care waste management?

options.A: To prevent infection and environmental harm
options.B: To create extra work for nursing staff
options.C: To reduce hospital running costs
options.D: To clear up floor space in wards

explanation: Managing medical waste safely stops the spread of disease and protects both hospital workers and the outside community from dangerous materials. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h1)

question: What is the main difference between an acute kidney injury and chronic renal failure?

options.A: Chronic renal failure always resolves completely with proper hydration therapy.
options.B: Acute injury develops slowly over several years without causing any symptoms.
options.C: Acute injury only affects the bladder, while chronic failure affects the entire ureter.
options.D: Chronic renal failure involves permanent and irreversible loss of nephron function.

explanation: You've got this! Chronic renal failure causes permanent scarring and loss of nephrons over time. Acute injury, on the other hand, can often be reversed if caught early. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T7#GNS213_U4_T7_h1)

question: What is a practical solution for QA committees when computers and digital health records are not available?

options.A: Ignoring clinical data collection entirely
options.B: Using simple, well-designed paper tracking tools and logs
options.C: Stopping all quality checks until computers are donated
options.D: Waiting for patients to remember their own medical histories

explanation: You nailed it! Good paper-based logs keep quality assurance running smoothly even when technology is missing. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h8)

question: Why do nurses always do a double-check before giving high-risk medications?

options.A: To eliminate the need for patient wristband scanning
options.B: To catch calculation or transcription errors before administration
options.C: To reduce the time spent documenting on the computer
options.D: To comply with insurance billing requirements for intensive care

explanation: Having a second pair of eyes helps catch little math or dosage mistakes that anyone could miss when tired. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T7#GNS113_U2_T7_h4)

question: A local government wants nurses to happily stay long-term in remote health posts. Which step is most effective?

options.A: Reducing the operational hours of remote clinics to twice a week
options.B: Threatening to dismiss any nurse who requests a transfer to an urban center
options.C: Eliminating all training programs to keep staff working on site full-time
options.D: Providing staff quarters, hardship allowances, and regular promotion opportunities

explanation: Taking care of staff needs—like providing a place to live and rewarding their hard work—makes them want to stay and serve the community. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T4#GNS124_U2_T4_h6)

question: How do newborn babies mostly make body heat when they get cold?

options.A: Through vigorous involuntary shivering
options.B: By metabolizing brown adipose tissue
options.C: By activating sweat gland secretions
options.D: Through rapid skeletal muscle contraction

explanation: Babies can't shiver like adults do! Instead, they burn a special kind of fat called brown fat (adipose tissue) to stay warm. It's a neat trick, but it uses up a lot of energy. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h2)

question: What is the physical state of saturated fats, like butter, at room temperature?

options.A: Liquid
options.B: Solid
options.C: Vaporized
options.D: Gaseous

explanation: Saturated fats like butter and palm oil stay firm or solid at room temperature because of their tight chemical structure. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T005#GNS227_U6_T005_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a goal of a true patient safety culture in a hospital?

options.A: Promoting collaborative teamwork across doctors and nurses
options.B: Finding root systemic causes when unexpected complications occur
options.C: Punishing individual staff members immediately for every minor mistake
options.D: Encouraging open discussion about accidental clinical errors

explanation: Blaming staff for minor errors creates fear, which stops people from reporting safety issues. A true safety culture focuses on learning! [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h7)

question: Why do clinical nurses need to understand the basics of diet and nutrition?

options.A: It allows nurses to support recovery and identify early malnutrition
options.B: It helps nurses prescribe complex surgical procedures independently
options.C: It replaces the need for professional hospital dietitians entirely
options.D: It enables nurses to manufacture synthetic vitamins at the bedside

explanation: Knowing your nutrition helps you spot early signs of poor feeding in patients and guide them toward a faster recovery! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T003#GNS227_U4_T003_h1)

question: Why is simple health information alone often insufficient to change community habits?

options.A: Diseases change faster than educational pamphlets can print
options.B: People are also influenced by cultural beliefs and social norms
options.C: Health messages are always written in difficult medical terms
options.D: Community members never trust trained health professionals

explanation: Human behavior is shaped by culture, tradition, and community pressure, requiring interactive communication rather than simple lecturing. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T4#GNS225_U2_T4_h7)

question: What happens during qualitative data analysis?

options.A: Patients fill out numerical rating scales for pain
options.B: Computers calculate complex algebraic formulas and p-values
options.C: Researchers code text to identify recurring themes and patterns
options.D: Blood samples are centrifuged in a hospital laboratory

explanation: Qualitative analysis organizes narrative words and interviews into meaningful categories or themes. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the very first thing you should do after an accidental needle-stick injury?

options.A: Cover the bleeding wound tightly with a waterproof bandage
options.B: Squeeze the puncture site firmly to force out old blood
options.C: Wash the affected area thoroughly with soap and water
options.D: Apply a strong antiseptic alcohol solution to seal the cut

explanation: Spot on! Don't panic. Calmly wash the area right away with plenty of soap and running water to flush out as many germs as possible. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h7)

question: What question does a healthcare organization's mission statement primarily answer?

options.A: How many patient beds will we add in twenty years?
options.B: Which staff members deserve a promotion this month?
options.C: Why do we exist right now and who do we serve?
options.D: What will our total financial budget be next year?

explanation: The mission statement defines the current purpose and core activities of the healthcare facility. [learn more](GST321_U2_T3#GST321_U2_T3_h2)

question: How does the growing baby and uterus contribute to constipation later in pregnancy?

options.A: By increasing the production of digestive enzymes
options.B: By putting direct mechanical pressure on the bowels
options.C: By completely stopping the production of stomach acid
options.D: By speeding up the movement of food through the colon

explanation: Exactly! As the baby grows, there is less space in the tummy, and the heavy uterus presses right against the intestines, slowing things down. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h2)

question: What happens to a patient's red blood cells if they are given a severely hypotonic intravenous solution?

options.A: They remain completely unchanged
options.B: They immediately multiply rapidly
options.C: They swell and may burst
options.D: They shrink and shrivel up

explanation: In a hypotonic solution, water rushes into the cells because the surrounding fluid has a lower solute concentration, causing the cells to swell and potentially rupture (lysis). [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h6)

question: What is a common challenge hospitals face regarding waste management in resource-limited settings?

options.A: A complete absence of patients generating any hazardous waste
options.B: An overwhelming surplus of high-tech microwave sterilization units
options.C: Excessive funding that leads to over-purchasing of medical bins
options.D: Erratic power supply and scarcity of specialized color-coded bags

explanation: Spot on! Power cuts and shortages of proper bags make safe waste sorting a real challenge in many local facilities. Keep up the good work! [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h8)

question: Why do nurses track balancing measures during an improvement project?

options.A: To detect any unintended negative consequences in other parts of the system
options.B: To compare the hospital performance against international standards
options.C: To balance the nursing unit's monthly financial budget and payroll
options.D: To ensure that doctors and nurses work the exact same number of hours

explanation: Brilliant! Balancing measures act like an early warning system to make sure fixing one problem doesn't accidentally cause another one somewhere else. [learn more](GST319_U3_T1#GST319_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is a common misconception patients sometimes hold about essential drugs?

options.A: They think essential drugs are only sold in overseas luxury clinics
options.B: They refuse to take them because they taste too sweet
options.C: They assume essential drugs can cure every known genetic disorder
options.D: They believe essential drugs are inferior because they are affordable

explanation: Because essential medicines are reasonably priced generics, some people wrongly assume they lack potency compared to expensive brands. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a good nursing practice when caring for a post-abortion patient with a weak immune system?

options.A: Maintaining strict aseptic techniques
options.B: Administering prescribed prophylactic antibiotics
options.C: Skipping hand hygiene between patients
options.D: Monitoring for subtle temperature spikes

explanation: Never skip hand hygiene! Clean hands are always a must, especially when caring for vulnerable patients who can easily catch infections. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T017#GNS226_U5_T017_h4)

question: What does the abbreviation SBAR stand for in clinical communication?

options.A: Safety, Briefing, Assessment, Review
options.B: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.C: Symptoms, Blood pressure, Activity, Rate
options.D: System, Bedside, Action, Record

explanation: You got it! SBAR is your trusty tool for sharing clear, snappy patient updates with doctors and fellow nurses. [learn more](GST321_U6_T1#GST321_U6_T1_h5)

question: What is a common traditional barrier to assertiveness in hospitals?

options.A: Excessive training on communication skills
options.B: A complete lack of clinical handovers
options.C: Too many patient safety checklists
options.D: Strict medical hierarchy and fear of punishment

explanation: Traditional power structures often punish junior staff who question authority, creating fear around speaking up. [learn more](GST321_U7_T5#GST321_U7_T5_h4)

question: What important step must a nurse take before transferring an obstetric emergency patient to a bigger hospital?

options.A: Wait until the patient's family fully pays all hospital bills in advance
options.B: Perform a major surgical operation at the primary clinic before transfer
options.C: Advise the patient to walk to the nearest main road to find a commercial taxi
options.D: Stabilize the patient's condition and write a clear referral note detailing care provided

explanation: Always stabilize what you can and write a clear handover note so the receiving team knows what has already been done! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h8)

question: When caring for a patient at home who isn't eating well, what is a common mistake people make?

options.A: It is usually mistaken for simple lack of appetite instead of deeper physical or mental issues.
options.B: It is almost always caused by a lack of fresh water in the home.
options.C: It is primarily due to patients intentionally fasting for religious reasons.
options.D: It is rarely encountered by nurses working outside of hospitals.

explanation: It's easy to assume a patient just doesn't feel like eating, but usually there's a deeper physical or emotional reason hiding underneath. You'll spot these clues as you care for them! [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h1)

question: Why does the infection control team monitor how well hospital surfaces are cleaned?

options.A: To make sure the hospital floors always shine brightly for visiting inspectors
options.B: Because many harmful pathogens can survive on dry hospital surfaces for long periods
options.C: To keep the housekeeping department busy between their regular meal breaks
options.D: Because cleaning chemicals are expensive and must be rationed carefully

explanation: Correct! Germs can hide out on bedrails, trays, and tables for ages if we don't clean them properly. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h7)

question: Which data collection method involves walking through the community to visually inspect environmental conditions?

options.A: Laboratory testing
options.B: Structured survey
options.C: Key informant interview
options.D: Observation

explanation: Observation or windshield surveys allow nurses to physically see housing conditions, water sources, and waste disposal practices. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h3)

question: What makes an 'android' pelvis shape stand out?

options.A: It is heart-shaped with prominent ischial spines
options.B: It is narrow and oval with a very long front-to-back measurement
options.C: It is flat and wide with a short front-to-back diameter
options.D: It is a classic round shape found in most females

explanation: An android pelvis is more like a male pelvis, featuring a heart-shaped opening that can sometimes make labor a bit tricky. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T10#GNS121_U5_T10_h5)

question: Which connective tissue layer wraps around an entire skeletal muscle?

options.A: Perimysium
options.B: Periosteum
options.C: Endomysium
options.D: Epimysium

explanation: Think of the epimysium as the tough outer coat that wraps up the whole muscle, keeping it safe and secure! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h2)

question: What is the main goal when treating a patient who has amenorrhoea?

options.A: Surgically removing the ovaries to stop hormone swings
options.B: Immediately restoring natural fertility in every case
options.C: Treating the specific underlying root cause
options.D: Preventing future pregnancy with strong contraceptives

explanation: Because amenorrhoea is a sign of something else, our treatment focuses on fixing the root problem—whether it is lifestyle, hormones, or anatomy. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T4#GNS216_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why should you, as a nurse, look beyond just the sick patient and check on the whole household?

options.A: Patients never feel stressed if medical staff are around
options.B: Nurses are legally required to counsel all relatives
options.C: When one person gets sick, it stresses everyone else out too
options.D: Hospital rules say family members must pay all bills directly

explanation: Illness doesn't happen in a vacuum. When a family member falls sick, it creates a ripple effect of worry and stress for everyone close to them. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT something a home care nurse tracks when evaluating a client's progress?

options.A: Tracking how many television channels the client watches daily
options.B: Monitoring whether vital signs like blood pressure are stabilizing
options.C: Assessing whether surgical or chronic wounds are healing properly
options.D: Observing if functional abilities like walking are improving

explanation: Spot on! We focus on health stats, wound healing, and daily strength—not how much TV they watch! [learn more](GNS324_U1_T3#GNS324_U1_T3_h7)

question: Why is keeping a close eye on vital signs so crucial when a patient is going through alcohol or sedative withdrawal?

options.A: It helps prove to the patient that they have an active drug problem
options.B: It replaces the need to take blood samples for kidney function tests
options.C: Withdrawal from these substances can cause dangerous and life-threatening physical instability
options.D: Vital signs remain completely normal throughout the entire detox process

explanation: Spot on! Unlike some other substances, alcohol and sedative withdrawal can trigger severe seizures and drastic blood pressure changes. Close monitoring keeps the patient safe. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T4#GNS313_U3_T4_h5)

question: Why should a community health nurse look at the health needs of a whole group instead of just single patients?

options.A: It helps allocate resources effectively to design meaningful programs
options.B: It guarantees complete eradication of all chronic diseases
options.C: It eliminates the need to ever visit individual households
options.D: It ensures every single citizen receives specialized surgery

explanation: Looking at the big picture helps you focus on what really plagues the population so you can put your limited time and materials to the best possible use! [learn more](GNS124_U3_T2#GNS124_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why is a one-time training workshop at the start of a project not enough for long-term success?

options.A: New staff constantly join the ward and need to learn the protocols too
options.B: Hospital rules forbid nurses from attending more than one workshop
options.C: Initial workshops never cover the correct clinical procedures
options.D: Staff members forget everything they learned within the first hour

explanation: High staff turnover means continuous, ongoing education is essential so new arrivals understand and follow established practices. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h5)

question: A community nurse crosses their arms and looks at the floor while a client talks about their illness. What is the most likely effect of this behavior?

options.A: The client may feel ignored and stop sharing important details
options.B: The client will feel encouraged to ask more questions
options.C: The client will better understand their medication schedule
options.D: The client will appreciate the nurse saving time

explanation: Closed body language and lack of eye contact signal disinterest or judgment, which makes clients reluctant to open up. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h3)

question: Why must a nurse researcher use a descriptive design before starting an experimental trial?

options.A: Because descriptive data helps establish basic baseline knowledge about a problem
options.B: Because ethical boards legally forbid any nursing experiments without surveys
options.C: Because descriptive designs are the only way to get funding from hospitals
options.D: Because experiments always fail if they do not include a questionnaire

explanation: You cannot fix a problem if you don't first understand it! Descriptive work gives us that essential starting picture before we try out new treatments. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h1)

question: A patient with severe malnutrition is admitted to your ward. Why are they at high risk for opportunistic infections?

options.A: Poor nutrition compromises their immune defenses and breaks down physical barriers
options.B: Lack of nutrients stops medications from working inside the bloodstream
options.C: Their body temperature permanently rises to a level that fosters bacterial growth
options.D: Malnourished tissues attract higher concentrations of ambient airborne viruses

explanation: Good clinical thinking! Without proper food and nutrients, the body cannot build strong immune cells or maintain tough physical barriers like skin and mucous membranes. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T3#GNS313_U1_T3_h3)

question: Why is proper patient allocation so important during staffing?

options.A: It ensures everyone works the exact same night shifts
options.B: It eliminates the need for shift handovers
options.C: It matches staff skills and experience with patient care needs
options.D: It guarantees hospital operating costs stay at zero

explanation: Matching the right nurse to the right patient keeps everyone safe and prevents junior nurses from feeling overwhelmed. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h4)

question: A patient asks how Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) works. How should you explain it?

options.A: It builds a chemical defense in your body so the virus cannot establish an infection if you are exposed
options.B: It permanently boosts your natural red blood cell count to fight off germs
options.C: It numbs nerve endings so you no longer feel any pain during intercourse
options.D: It cures any existing HIV infection within the first week of daily dosing

explanation: You got it! PrEP gives the body a protective chemical shield so the virus can't take hold if exposure happens. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T9#GNS216_U6_T9_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of disease surveillance in public health?

options.A: Conducting laboratory research on new medications
options.B: Treating individual patients in hospital wards
options.C: Tracking health data to guide planning and action
options.D: Managing hospital financial budgets and staff

explanation: Surveillance focuses on collecting and analyzing population health data so authorities can take proper action to protect the public. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h1)

question: What happens when infectious waste is mistakenly thrown into a regular household waste bin?

options.A: The organic material neutralizes all bacterial pathogens within an hour
options.B: The sorting machine at the dumpsite automatically separates the items
options.C: The entire batch of waste becomes contaminated and must be handled as hazardous
options.D: The local municipal workers will clean and recycle the infectious materials

explanation: You got it! Mixing just one infectious item with general rubbish ruins the whole batch and puts people at risk. Careful sorting is key! [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h4)

question: Which statement is true about Type IV FGM?

options.A: It still poses serious risks of bleeding, pain, and infection
options.B: It is always performed by licensed medical doctors
options.C: It is universally recognized as a form of childbirth preparation
options.D: It carries no risk of infection because it is minor

explanation: Correct! Even though Type IV uses different methods like piercing or scraping, any non-medical cutting of genital tissue carries high risks. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h6)

question: Which inhalation device requires the patient to take a fast, forceful breath to activate medication delivery?

options.A: Dry Powder Inhaler
options.B: Metered-dose inhaler with spacer
options.C: Simple nasal cannula
options.D: Standard nebulizer machine

explanation: Dry Powder Inhalers rely entirely on the patient's own inhalation effort to pull the powder out of the device and into the lungs. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is the main goal of the Essential Drug Programme in public health?

options.A: Ensuring safe and affordable medicines are always available
options.B: Eliminating the need for doctors in rural clinics
options.C: Reducing the overall salaries of hospital pharmacy staff
options.D: Promoting only foreign-manufactured pharmaceutical brands

explanation: You got this! The whole point of the Essential Drug Programme is to make sure vital, quality medicines remain easy to get and affordable for everyone. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T6#GNS215_U1_T6_h1)

question: What do the letters in the SMART goal-setting framework stand for?

options.A: Simple, Medical, Active, Realistic, Total
options.B: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound
options.C: Safe, Meaningful, Accessible, Rapid, Tender
options.D: Systematic, Manual, Analytical, Routine, Tested

question: Why do nurse researchers find ogive graphs useful when looking at health data?

question: What does a community action plan typically include?

question: A patient says, 'My cough is gone after a month, so I want to stop my TB pills.' What is your best response as a nurse?

question: How does an emotionally intelligent nurse leader handle a dispute between two staff members?

question: In disaster triage systems like START, what does the color RED mean?

question: Which of these is a clear example of vector-borne transmission?

question: What is the primary function of the amygdala within the limbic system?

question: What is a big plus of having homestead gardens in rural areas?

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to prevent software-related mistakes on the ward?

question: What must a nurse always do before starting any care in a patient's home?

question: Which nutrient is especially critical for adolescent girls and boys during major growth spurts to support expanding blood volume?

question: According to the Spaulding classification, how must you process a medical tool that goes deep inside sterile body tissues?

question: A researcher targets prisoners for a risky drug trial just because they are locked up and easy to reach. Which ethical rule is being broken?

question: What is the primary significance of traditional West African medicine in modern pharmacology?

question: What control measure involves replacing a toxic chemical with a harmless water-based cleaner?

question: A community nurse needs a quick, easy way to check for sudden fluid loss or weight gain in an adult. What should they use?

question: Why should you NOT send a patient with a blocked airway for a CT scan right away?

options.C: Contrast dye makes the vocal cords snap shut.

question: What is 'data architecture' when talking about Electronic Health Records?

question: A patient comes in with a severe pain crisis, but their oxygen saturation is completely normal at 98% on room air. What should you do about oxygen therapy?

options.A: Administer high-flow oxygen immediately to reverse the bone pain
options.B: Place the patient on a non-rebreather mask to prevent acute chest syndrome

question: How can experiencing a severe illness during childhood affect a person later in life?

question: How does hospice philosophy view the dying process?

options.D: As a medical failure that must be fought at all costs

question: Why do we test changes on a small scale during the 'Do' phase of a project?

question: Which type of sexually transmitted infection can usually be cured with antibiotics?

question: What simple inventory rule helps nurses make sure older ward medications are used before they expire?

question: What is the main focus of Psychological First Aid (PFA) right after a disaster?

options.B: Forcing survivors to recount every detail of the traumatic event
options.C: Providing humane comfort, safety, and practical support

question: What is the main role of ATP in the body?

options.A: Transporting oxygen molecules directly to the brain cells
options.B: Regulating the total volume of blood in circulation
options.C: Serving as the primary energy currency for cellular work
options.D: Acting as a structural support fiber for major organs

question: When is a recessive trait expressed in an individual?

question: What is the primary purpose of an after-action review (AAR) following a disaster?

question: What is the primary focus of clinical nursing informatics?

question: A community health nurse wants to help lower the rate of undiagnosed high blood pressure in a low-income neighborhood. Which activity is the best initial approach?

question: How does trial leave differ mainly from occasional leave?

question: What is the main goal of mitigation in disaster management?

question: Which antibody class shows up first at the very beginning of a brand-new infection?

question: During a disease outbreak, which of these is a core duty for a community health nurse?

options.C: Conducting contact tracing and educating community members on prevention

question: Why might you suggest a patient eating plant-based iron (like beans or greens) drink a glass of orange juice with their meal?

question: Why is the "action line" on a partograph so critical for your clinical decisions?

question: Which factor is most critical for ensuring the long-term sustainability of a community health project?

question: What happens during the process of clot retraction?

question: How is droplet transmission different from airborne transmission?

question: If a patient has a very weak immune system, which type of drug do they urgently need to fight an infection?

question: A clinic is starting a digital triage system but keeps paper registers nearby just in case the network goes down. What is this strategy called?

question: How does dietetics mainly differ from general nutrition study?

question: Why should nurse researchers avoid using 3D visual effects on bar charts?

question: Blood-injection-injury phobias are quite unique. What physical reaction makes them different from other phobias?

question: In community health nursing, who is considered your primary client?

question: What are the two main gonadotropins released by the anterior pituitary gland?

question: Why do nurse researchers need to know the different tiers of literature sources?

question: What is the main use of the International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) questionnaire?

question: What happens to systemic blood pressure when arterioles undergo widespread vasoconstriction?

question: Which of these clinical situations is a classic reason to order an EPS?

question: Where should a completed incident report be submitted in the hospital?

question: How does bovine mastitis (udder infection) directly affect raw milk?

question: Which tool is specifically used to check a patient's risk of falling?

question: Which factor directly causes a sudden drop in foetal oxygen due to mechanical compression?

options.B: Maternal mild anaemia

options.D: Advanced maternal age

question: A patient with chronic kidney disease shows signs of metabolic acidosis. What lab result would a nurse expect to see?

options.C: A high concentration of bicarbonate in the fresh urine
options.D: A low serum bicarbonate level on the lab report

question: What can happen if strong corticosteroid creams are used on thin skin areas for too long?

options.B: Skin thinning and atrophy

options.D: Complete numbness of the local nerves

question: Which electrical shift makes the heart muscle cells contract?

options.B: Repolarization

options.D: Polarization

question: Why is the inner forearm a preferred site for routine tuberculosis skin tests?

options.C: It contains thick subcutaneous fat that cushions the needle.
options.D: It absorbs medications much faster than other body parts.

question: Which core value means respecting a patient's right to make their own choices about their body and care?

options.A: Autonomy
options.B: Veracity
options.C: Beneficence
options.D: Justice

question: What is the primary purpose of using orthopedic traction?

options.A: To apply a pulling force to align bones and reduce spasms

options.C: To permanently replace damaged joint cartilage without surgery
options.D: To deliver strong local pain medication directly into a fracture

question: When a mistake happens, why does a systems thinker look beyond the person who made it?

options.A: To prove that the nursing staff had too many tasks to complete

options.C: To understand how the environment and processes allowed the error
options.D: To make sure the hospital avoids paying any financial penalties

explanation: Blaming an individual often hides the real structural and environmental weaknesses that let the error happen in the first place. Every nurse makes mistakes; looking at the system helps us fix the root cause so you can practice safely! [learn more](GST319_U2_T6#GST319_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why is the PDSA cycle so helpful in Nigerian healthcare settings with limited resources?

question: Why can it cause trouble if an NGO runs a health project without involving local health authorities?

options.D: The clinic will automatically become a profit-making business

question: Which principle ensures that clinic operating hours and locations work well for students?

question: What is a common reason why busy nurses might resist new quality improvement ideas?

options.C: They are legally barred from participating in hospital management

question: Why does the internal urethral sphincter need to close tightly during emission?

question: Which diagnostic test specifically records the electrical activity of the brain?

options.A: Electrocardiogram (ECG)

question: In pharmacokinetics, what does the letter 'A' stand for in the famous ADME acronym?

question: What is the primary goal of palliative care for an older adult near the end of life?

options.A: Relief of pain and enhancement of comfort

options.C: Prevention of normal age-related eye changes
options.D: Aggressive cure of underlying terminal illnesses

question: Which team member takes the lead in evaluating a resident's nutrition and managing special diets?

options.A: Registered dietitian
options.B: Social worker

explanation: Registered dietitians assess nutrition needs, track weight changes, and design healthy meal plans tailored to each resident. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h5)

question: How should a normal optic disc appear during a fundus examination?

question: What does a Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM) tell you?

options.A: The exact number of doses remaining inside the glass vial

options.C: Whether the vaccine container has been contaminated with bacteria
options.D: The precise manufacturing date printed on the cardboard box

question: A client with active breast cancer asks for an injectable contraceptive. How is this classified under WHO guidelines?

question: Which method ranks highest in the hierarchy of hazard controls?

options.A: Work practice training

question: Why do we use computer software in clinical nursing today?

options.A: To replace the need for professional clinical judgment entirely

options.C: To increase the time nurses spend filling out paper documents
options.D: To eliminate the requirement for direct patient interaction

explanation: You've got this! Software tools are just there to help make your data handling easier and more accurate, giving you more time for what really matters—caring for your patients. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h1)

question: What happens in the body when there aren't enough antioxidant micronutrients to protect the cells?

options.A: Enhanced cell membrane stability
options.B: Immediate hormone hypersecretion
options.C: Rapid muscle fiber regeneration
options.D: Oxidative stress and cell damage

explanation: Well done! Without antioxidants to keep harmful free radicals in check, those unstable molecules cause tissue wear-and-tear and lead to long-term health issues. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T13#GNS313_U2_T13_h3)

question: Who usually chairs the Local Government Area PHC Development Committee?

options.A: The LGA Chairman or health supervisor

question: Why should we make sure marginalized or vulnerable groups have a voice in community health committees?

options.D: It is the only way to meet nursing licensure requirements

question: Which sign is a classic clue that a teenager might be dealing with iron deficiency anemia?

question: What is the main ethical goal of triage when a mass disaster happens?

options.A: Saving the most critically ill patient first, regardless of resource consumption.

options.C: Providing the greatest good for the greatest number of people using available resources.
options.D: Treating every patient in the exact order they arrived at the hospital.

explanation: Exactly! Disaster triage flips routine care on its head: instead of focusing only on the sickest individual, you focus on saving as many lives as possible with what you have. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T2#GNS315_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is another common name for cancellous bone?

question: Who is protected when a nurse properly uses isolation precautions?

options.A: Only the doctors working in the ward

question: Why can diagnosing an emerging infection be very difficult during the early stages?

question: How can nurses use data collected from post-disaster surveys and feedback sessions?

question: Which of these is one of the most common types of errors in clinical practice?

question: A nurse treats a high blood pressure patient living in a neighborhood with poor food access. What is the best all-round approach?

question: What is the main use of 'process mapping' in quality improvement?

question: What is the primary purpose of applying antibiotic eye ointment to a newborn shortly after birth?

question: Which ethical principle simply means a nurse or researcher must 'do no harm' to study participants?

question: Which of these is NOT a challenge facing adolescent reproductive healthcare in Nigeria?

question: Why do nurses commonly use local heat or cold applications?

question: A psychiatric nurse is caring for someone starting a new antipsychotic medication. What is a key nursing duty here?

options.A: Assuming the medication will cure the social crisis causing the illness

options.C: Monitoring for medication side effects and educating the family on adherence

question: What do we call it when a hospital ward slowly slips back into old, messy habits after an improvement project finishes?

question: Why is 'operational scalability' so important for a Rapid Response Center?

question: An adolescent health clinic welcomes all teenagers regardless of their financial status or background. Which core characteristic is this clinic showing?

question: Which of these is NOT a major challenge facing formal home health care in Nigeria?

question: What is your main responsibility as a nurse when a new clinical policy is introduced?

question: What is the primary public health goal of proper food storage?

question: Why is letting family members help with basic comfort care so beneficial for them?

question: Why do healthcare workers worry so much about carbapenem-resistant germs?

question: In the human female reproductive tract, where does fertilization usually happen?

question: How does low health literacy make everyday nursing care more challenging?

options.B: Patients refuse to speak with doctors of any specialty

question: Why would a doctor order a stool culture for a patient with ongoing diarrhoea?

question: Why do hospital disaster plans include steps for safely discharging stable patients?

question: What is the scientific term used for parasitic worms in medical practice?

question: An emergency patient needs medicine right now. Which route will work the fastest?

question: Why should nurses understand how different healthcare sectors work?

question: What is the main hormone behind most skin changes during pregnancy?

question: What common belief often drives high injection rates among patients in many local communities?

question: Which of these is a major operational headache for many voluntary health agencies?

question: A nurse wants to understand why mothers in a village refuse to bring children for immunization. Which method is most suitable?

question: Why do we connect our new research findings back to older, published studies?

question: What is the main purpose of an action plan during a project?

question: What type of medicine is often given to hospitalized COVID-19 patients to prevent blood clots?

question: What is the main job of the cerebrospinal fluid that surrounds the brain?

question: Why should nurses involve local community leaders when starting health programs?

question: What is the main feature of a fixed cost in a hospital?

question: How does a Clinical Decision Support (CDS) feature protect hospitalized patients?

question: Which part of the reflex arc carries the electrical signal away from the spinal cord to the target muscle or gland?

question: What is a transect walk during an environmental scan?

options.C: A laboratory test used to measure water contamination levels

question: Giving routine childhood vaccinations to prevent measles is an example of which level of prevention?

question: What happens to the body during a state of positive energy balance?

question: Why are Information Retrieval Systems necessary for modern clinical practice?

question: In a standard 28-day menstrual cycle, around which day does ovulation usually happen?

question: How do intestinal parasite eggs most commonly spread to people?

question: Which of the following is an example of a three-dimensional instructional aid?

question: Why is following a strict code of ethics so important for a nurse?

question: How should a nurse handle a cultural food taboo that limits a pregnant woman's protein intake?

question: What is the main reason nurses make sure hospital patients have clean, trimmed nails?

question: Why is continuous re-evaluation necessary in emergency nursing care?

question: What is the typical pattern of pain experienced in the early stages of osteoarthritis?

question: As a nurse, why shouldn't you focus only on the physical symptoms of a blood disorder?

question: Which measure helps protect ordinary citizens from going broke paying for medical care?

question: Why is it important to treat chronic pain promptly in a physically disabled patient?

question: Why does severe liver disease (cirrhosis) often lead to higher levels of active oral drugs in the bloodstream?

question: When should you NEVER perform routine eye irrigation?

question: Which of the following is a key performance indicator used to evaluate directing effectiveness?

question: Which of the following is NOT a common consequence of relying solely on a free market for healthcare?

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical duty of a nurse working in a community mental health center?

options.A: Administering long-acting injectable psychiatric medications
options.B: Performing major neurosurgery for treatment-resistant depression
options.C: Connecting vulnerable clients with local housing and food resources
options.D: Providing psychoeducation to patients and their family members

explanation: Nurses in community settings do not perform neurosurgery; their role focuses on support, education, medication management, and resource linkage. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h7)

question: A patient is upset after getting the wrong test. What is the best way to talk to them first?

options.A: Tell them to speak only to the legal department outside the hospital
options.B: Acknowledge their frustration, listen to their concerns, and explain the next steps
options.C: Tell them that mistakes happen to everyone and they should not worry
options.D: Threaten to discharge them if they continue asking questions

explanation: Validating their feelings builds trust! Letting them know you hear them is a core part of professional nursing care. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h5)

question: Why are overfilled sharps containers dangerous on the ward?

options.A: They attract insects and rodents into patient care areas
options.B: They release toxic chemical fumes into the nursing station
options.C: They expose workers to protruding needles and unstable sharp items
options.D: They prevent the automated counting of used syringes

explanation: Once a sharps box is past its fill line, needles start stacking up near the top and can easily prick the next person trying to dispose of waste. Close them on time! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why can a sudden infection mess up the results of a patient's blood protein test?

options.A: Infections trigger body changes that alter protein levels regardless of diet
options.B: Lab technicians are not allowed to run protein tests during an illness
options.C: Infections destroy all blood drawing needles in the clinic
options.D: Infection automatically cures any existing vitamin deficiency

explanation: Inflammation from an infection can drive blood protein levels down, which might trick you into thinking the patient is starving when they actually have an infection. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T19#GNS214_U1_T19_h5)

question: How would you simply describe an autoimmune disease?

options.A: A condition where the immune system attacks the body's own healthy tissues
options.B: A temporary infection spread through close contact in a community
options.C: An immediate allergic reaction caused by exposure to environmental pollen
options.D: A genetic deficiency that prevents the production of red blood cells

explanation: In autoimmune diseases, the immune system gets confused and mistakenly treats friendly, healthy body cells as enemies, attacking them by mistake. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h7)

question: How can we best describe a 'system' in a busy healthcare setting?

options.A: Interdependent parts working together to achieve a common goal
options.B: A single computer program used to record daily patient vitals
options.C: An isolated department that operates entirely on its own
options.D: The strict disciplinary rules enforced by the hospital director

explanation: Think of a hospital like a football team: every department connects with and relies on the others to make sure the patient gets better safely. [learn more](GST319_U2_T7#GST319_U2_T7_h3)

question: What is the big advantage of modern low-osmolality ORS compared to the older, stronger formula?

options.A: It reduces stool volume and the need for IV fluids
options.B: It provides all the daily vitamins a growing child needs
options.C: It tastes much sweeter and dissolves instantly in cold water
options.D: It cures bacterial infections without needing antibiotics

explanation: By lowering the sugar and salt slightly, the modern formula creates less osmotic pull in the gut, which means less watery stool and fewer trips to the hospital for drips! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h4)

question: What is the main focus of epidemiology in healthcare?

options.A: Treating rare surgical conditions in tertiary hospitals
options.B: Managing hospital finances and staff rosters
options.C: Performing laboratory tests on individual blood samples
options.D: Studying how and why diseases occur in populations

explanation: Spot on! While bedside nursing looks at one patient at a time, epidemiology zooms out to look at health patterns across entire communities. You've got this! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h1)

question: When doing a quick ABCDE emergency check on a patient, what does the letter 'C' stand for?

options.A: Coughing
options.B: Circulation
options.C: Consciousness
options.D: Cyanosis

explanation: A is Airway, B is Breathing, and C is Circulation! You check pulses and bleeding here. Easy peasy! [learn more](GNS315_U2_T3#GNS315_U2_T3_h6)
